Organized Phonology Data for Sop (Sob) Language. Ms, SIL, Ukarumpa'). I read both sheets in full: neither marks stress on any word in the inventories, syllable-pattern lists or the trans…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only published statements say stress is not phonemic (non-contrastive) and that there is no tone or length; neither SIL data sheet says where stress falls, so the placement is undescribed. Hedged wording ('does not seem'), draft status, no data.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The parallel Sob OPD (entry 42387, p. 3) says only 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic.' Z'graggen 1969: 13 says stress marking was omitted because the patterning had not been established.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level implied (a phonology data sheet on citation forms of words); no stress marks in the wordlist or in the transcribed text, so nothing about phrase-level accent either.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2011 Usino OPD describes the Apamore dialect of Sop (Usino) [urw] (villages Usino, Apamore; data checked by P. Lillie); the 2004 Sob OPD describes Sop (Sob, Usino) at Usino village (based on Gasaway 1994). Both fall under sopp1247; Glottolog lists no dialect glottocodes. Older names Kari / Usino (Z'graggen 1969: Usur Group; Claassen & McElhanon 1970: Usino Family).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/252971)
sources.note: Classification and comparative forms (Usino = B14, Peka Family); no occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'phonology'. Silent.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/254286)
sources.note: Sec. 6.1 (p. 66) gives stress remarks only for Finisterre languages ('Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat') and for Suroi ('stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words'); nothing on Usino/Sop stress (Usino appears only in classification sec. 3.1 and possession-marking remarks sec. 6.2).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp. (hdl 1885/130077)
sources.note: p. 13: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Usino section 2.21.21.1 (p. 61) and the typological features of the Usur Group and Madang Phylum (pp. 62-69) say nothing about stress; only notes a high central vowel observed only in Usino.
